knowledge:
- key_parameters: path=The directory path containing the raw .idat files used in getBarcodes and getMethyLumiSet ;; barcodes=A character vector of specific barcodes to process in getMethyLumiSet ;; norm=The normalization method to apply in preprocess (e.g., 'illumina', 'SWAN', 'dasen') or the label for the plot in panelPlots ;; bg.corr=A logical indicating whether to perform background correction in preprocess ;; getSNparams arguments=Takes a MethyLumiSet object, the channel type ('M' for methylated, 'U' for unmethylated), and the probe type ('I-red', 'I-green', or 'II') ;; panelPlots arguments=Takes the MethyLumiSet object, three lists of skew-normal models (I-red, I-green, II), and optional parameters like plot='frames', frame.nums (vector of frame indices), and samp.num (integer index of the sample)
- alternatives: Standard preprocessing and normalization can be done directly via minfi or wateRmelon packages, but skewr is preferred when you want to visualize and evaluate these normalization effects in log2 intensity space using skew-normal mixture models.
- when_to_use: Use when performing quality control on Illumina 450k methylation array data, specifically to compare raw and normalized intensity distributions or to inspect the signal-to-noise ratio and probe-type biases.
- pitfalls: Fitting skew-normal mixture models to Type II intensity distributions (especially unmethylated probes) can be difficult and may perform poorly if the samples do not carry a reasonable assumption of purity ;; skewr is designed to process and plot an entire experiment; attempting to index a single sample and its models directly in the list arguments of panelPlots will fail. Instead, use the samp.num parameter or plot='frames' to isolate specific samples or frames ;; When constructing lists for panelPlots, the methylated models must always be listed first, followed by the unmethylated models (e.g., list(meth, unmeth)).

workflows.name: illumina_450k_qc_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Load raw Illumina 450k IDAT files, preprocess/normalize them, fit skew-normal mixture models to the intensity distributions, and generate diagnostic panel plots or single frame plots for quality control.
input: melon.raw (a MethyLumiSet object representing raw or loaded methylation data)
workflows.stages: 1. Retrieve barcodes from IDAT directory using getBarcodes ;; 2. Load raw data into a MethyLumiSet using getMethyLumiSet ;; 3. Preprocess/normalize the data using preprocess ;; 4. Estimate skew-normal mixture model parameters for methylated and unmethylated probes across Type I-red, Type I-green, and Type II subsets using getSNparams ;; 5. Group the mixture models into lists (methylated first, then unmethylated) ;; 6. Generate diagnostic panel plots or individual frame plots using panelPlots
workflows.code:
baseDir <- system.file("extdata/5723646052", package = "minfiData")
barcodes <- getBarcodes(path = baseDir)
methylumiset.raw <- getMethyLumiSet(path = baseDir, barcodes =  barcodes[1:2])
methylumiset.illumina <- preprocess(methylumiset.raw, norm = 'illumina',
                                    bg.corr = FALSE)
data(melon)
melon.raw <- melon[,11]
sn.raw.meth.I.red <- getSNparams(melon.raw, 'M', 'I-red')
sn.raw.unmeth.I.red <- getSNparams(melon.raw, 'U', 'I-red')
sn.raw.meth.I.green <- getSNparams(melon.raw, 'M', 'I-green')
sn.raw.unmeth.I.green <- getSNparams(melon.raw, 'U', 'I-green')
sn.raw.meth.II <- getSNparams(melon.raw, 'M', 'II')
sn.raw.unmeth.II <- getSNparams(melon.raw, 'U', 'II')
raw.I.red.mixes <- list(sn.raw.meth.I.red, sn.raw.unmeth.I.red)
raw.I.green.mixes <- list(sn.raw.meth.I.green, sn.raw.unmeth.I.green)
raw.II.mixes <- list(sn.raw.meth.II, sn.raw.unmeth.II)
panelPlots(melon.raw, raw.I.red.mixes, raw.I.green.mixes,
           raw.II.mixes, norm = 'Raw')
panelPlots(melon.raw, raw.I.red.mixes, raw.I.green.mixes,
           raw.II.mixes, plot='frames', frame.nums=c(1,3), norm='Raw')
